tier1_policy: Tier 1 requests are sent only on a scan that asks for active probes, at most once per target domain every 6 hours, and never to a domain whose verified owner turned active probes off.

rows.title: Document exists
rows.pass_when: https://{domain}/.well-known/poppy.json (or its www or apex sibling, see T0-SIB) answers 2xx, after at most 5 redirects, with a JSON object naming protocol_version or organization. A body sent as JSON that does not parse, is not an object or is over 100 KB also counts as found (and fails T0-03); a JSON object with neither key, an HTML page or any other body reads as no file

rows.title: Redirects safe
rows.pass_when: Every redirect hop on the way to poppy.json is HTTPS, and for a file declaring 0.3 or later the last URL's path is exactly /.well-known/poppy.json, with no query

rows.title: Valid JSON object
rows.pass_when: The body parses as a JSON object of at most 100 KB

rows.title: Supported protocol_version
rows.pass_when: protocol_version is a "major.minor" string Ora grades (0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 or 1.0), and the file is graded by that draft's rules. Before 1.0 an agent uses only a version it supports, so a later version Ora does not grade yet reads not tested. From 1.0 a later minor of the same major is compatible (spec 3.4), so a 1.x file is graded by the 1.0 rules, and a later major reads not tested with the rest graded by the Draft 1.0 rules. Ora follows Draft 1.0, still in progress, which the spec's authors ask builders to use; 0.4 is the latest published version. Before 1.0 neither a 1.0 agent nor a 0.4 agent uses the other's file, so each file is advised to reach both through supported_versions: a 1.0 file passes with an advisory unless it lists a 0.4 document, a 0.4 file unless it lists a 1.0 document (or moves to 1.0), and a file declaring an older draft with an advisory to move to 1.0 (or, when it already links a 1.0 document, to link a 0.4 one too)

rows.title: Organization names its own host
rows.pass_when: organization has a name and a domain, and organization.domain is the host that served the file after any redirects, compared ignoring case only (a leading www. counts); from Draft 1.0 it carries that host's port when the port is not 443 (spec 3.1). A file declaring 0.1 is graded by Draft 0.1 instead: the host the agent requested, ignoring a leading www.

rows.title: Has an interface
rows.pass_when: The file has at least one interface: an agent object, a non-empty apis array or a web object. For a file declaring 0.4 or later, web.disabled needs agent or apis too

rows.title: Issuer identified

request.condition: when a file declaring 0.3 or later is served by the host its organization.domain names

rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, the issuer comes from the protected resource metadata of https://{organization.domain}, following redirects only within that domain. A 404, or metadata whose resource is that URL and which lists no authorization server, means no issuer, which passes unless auth.issuer, signed_in access or Mediated Sign-In needs one; one server is the issuer (auth.issuer, when set, names it); several need auth.issuer to name one of them. Any other answer fails, a rate limit or server error included, since an agent never falls back to the domain; a bot challenge reads blocked and metadata past Ora's 100 KB read cap reads not tested. For a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2: auth.issuer is set whenever agent, apis, feedback (0.2) or web.browser_session_endpoint is present, N/A when nothing needs sign-in

rows.title: All URLs HTTPS
rows.pass_when: Every URL field the spec defines, and every string in the file that carries a URL scheme, is an absolute https URL. A block that exists to carry its URL (feedback in 0.2 and 0.3, excluded_tasks in 0.3, tasks from 0.4) fails without it, and for a file declaring 0.4 or later (0.3 defines no supported_versions) every supported_versions URL is on the host that served poppy.json

rows.title: Published on the requested host

request.condition: when the requested host has no file and its homepage resolved to the sibling

rows.pass_when: Ora's lookup, not defined by the spec: poppy.json is served on the requested host itself, not only on its www or apex sibling

rows.title: Other version documents consistent

request.condition: when a file declaring 0.4 or later lists one on the host that served it; up to 3, no redirect followed

rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.4: for a file declaring 0.4 or later, each document supported_versions links to answers 200 with no redirect, since an agent must not follow one; declares the protocol_version it is listed under; has no supported_versions of its own; and names the same organization.domain and selects the same issuer as poppy.json, so a new version does not change the Company's identifier. Ora reads at most 3, each on the host that served poppy.json (T0-08 grades entries on another host). Blocked when a bot shield answers; not tested when a document is past Ora's 100 KB read cap or the Company's issuer is not known; N/A without supported_versions, when poppy.json fails a row an agent stops at, or for a file declaring 0.3 or earlier, whose drafts define no supported_versions

rows.title: Issuer metadata reachable

request.condition: when the file names an issuer, or from Draft 0.3 its domain's protected resource metadata does

rows.pass_when: The issuer's RFC 8414 metadata (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server for the issuer, following redirects only within the issuer's registrable domain) answers 200 with a JSON object. For a file declaring 0.2 or later, an issuer whose host resolves to a loopback, private, link-local or other non-public address fails (spec 3), since no agent may connect to it

rows.title: Issuer match
rows.pass_when: The metadata's issuer is exactly the issuer: auth.issuer, or from Draft 0.3 the one T0-07 found

rows.title: Domain binding
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, the metadata's protected_resources lists https://{organization.domain}, host case aside, with no path or trailing slash (from Draft 1.0 the domain, and so the entry, carries its port when that is not 443, spec 3.1). For a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2, its poppy_domains lists organization.domain, case insensitive

rows.title: Required endpoints
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, the metadata has https token_endpoint and revocation_endpoint, a grant_types_supported that includes refresh_token, plus authorization_endpoint when that list has authorization_code and device_authorization_endpoint when it has the device_code grant. For a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2: https token_endpoint and revocation_endpoint, plus authorization_endpoint when auth.direct is set and device_authorization_endpoint when auth.device is set

rows.title: Cache headers
rows.pass_when: Ora inference, graded P2, for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2: the issuer metadata response sends Cache-Control or Expires. The spec's caching SHOULD bound agents, not the Company, and Draft 0.3 removed it, so the row reads N/A from 0.3

rows.title: Signing algorithms valid
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, when the issuer metadata lists token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported (it may leave it out), the list includes ES256, which every Company accepts for client assertions, and never none; from Draft 1.0 it also includes PS384, which every Company accepts too (spec 4.1) (T0-34 grades the list's absence next to a JWT method). Draft 0.2: when it lists dpop_signing_alg_values_supported, the list includes ES256. N/A when the list is not given or the file declares 0.1

rows.title: Signing algorithm list advertised
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, when token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported lists private_key_jwt or client_secret_jwt, the issuer metadata also lists token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_supported, as RFC 8414 section 2 requires. Before Draft 1.0 an agent can still sign with ES256 without it, which every Company must accept (spec 4.1), but an agent that signs blindly uses PS384 (spec 4.1, 10.7) and cannot tell whether it is accepted; from Draft 1.0 every Company accepts both, so the list only restates the rule. Ora grades the gap as a warning, never failing the check. N/A when neither method is listed, or the file declares 0.1 or 0.2

rows.title: Same sign-in on every domain

request.target: each other domain the issuer binds (poppy_domains, or protected_resources from Draft 0.3): /.well-known/poppy.json
request.condition: when the issuer binding holds and the issuer lists other domains, at most 3

rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, every other domain in the issuer's protected_resources (the first 3) whose poppy.json names an issuer names the same one (with an advisory when it describes a scope both files list differently, spec 3.2 SHOULD), and for a file declaring 0.4 or later every such domain that lists a browser_session_endpoint sets web.unscoped the same way; a file that names none selects its issuer through its own protected resource metadata, which Ora does not fetch, and reads not tested. Draft 0.2: every other domain in poppy_domains whose poppy.json names the same issuer carries the same auth block (key and scope order aside). N/A when none does or the file declares 0.1

rows.title: No plain PKCE
rows.pass_when: code_challenge_methods_supported, when the metadata lists it, does not include plain

rows.title: Scopes defined
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, each Company defines its own scopes: every auth.scopes entry has a description, and every auth.scope_hints entry has a changes value and a boolean personal_data, and for a file declaring 0.4 or later web.unscoped comes with a browser_session_endpoint (N/A when none of these is set). For a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2: each sign-in type in auth (direct, device, mediated) lists scopes, each poppy:read, poppy:write or a key of auth.custom_scopes; every custom scope has a description and no poppy: prefix

rows.title: Mediated sign-in well formed
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, Mediated Sign-In is an extension: its version 1 entry has a non-empty fields list (each with a label, a boolean secret and a name that is no OAuth or extension parameter) and scopes, and the issuer's grant_types_supported lists its grant when the metadata was read (T0-24 grades it next to auth.disabled). For a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2: auth.mediated has an https endpoint, a non-empty fields list (each with a name, a label and a boolean secret) and scopes

rows.title: Extensions named correctly
rows.pass_when: Every extension name is one the protocol defines (operations; mediated-sign-in, links, disclosures and ucp from Draft 0.3; browser-control from Draft 0.4) or is prefixed with a domain (example.com/name), and every extension carries a version (from Draft 0.4, a list of entries that each carry one)

rows.title: Extensions advertised fully
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, extensions.operations has the version the draft defines, "2" in 0.3 and "3" from 0.4 (with no entry at that version, agents ignore it and the row reads N/A); from 0.4 an operations entry with an endpoint has an https one, and an operations endpoint comes with web.browser_session_endpoint (a browser-control entry without one is an advisory note). For a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2: operations version "1" and an https endpoint

rows.title: Switched off consistently
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3: auth.disabled, when set, is true or false, and a file that sets it to true lists neither the Mediated Sign-In extension nor a conversation entry with access set to signed_in; for a file declaring 0.4 or later, web.disabled set to true comes with no browser_session_endpoint. N/A when neither is set, or the file declares 0.1 or 0.2

rows.title: Offered scopes described
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, every scope in the issuer's scopes_supported (from Draft 0.4, also in the scopes_supported of the domain's protected resource metadata, which agents read with it) has a description, in auth.scopes or in the OAuth flows of a listed OpenAPI document, so an agent can ask for only what a task needs; a scope agents cannot request can be left out of those lists. The spec says SHOULD; Ora weighs it for user experience, so a gap warns and never fails the check. OpenID Connect's standard scopes (openid, profile, email, address, phone, offline_access) are skipped. Not tested when a scope is still undescribed and a listed OpenAPI document could not be read, or the file lists the UCP extension, whose profile may hold the description; N/A when there is no issuer, the lists name no other scope, or the file declares 0.1 or 0.2

rows.title: Browser sign-in scope listed
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.4: when the file lists web.browser_session_endpoint and the Company offers sign-in, poppy:browser-sign-in is in the issuer's scopes_supported or the scopes_supported of the domain's protected resource metadata (section 3.2 allows either or both, and agents read them as one list). The Company must support that scope (section 6) and should list every scope an agent can request (section 3.2), so a missing entry warns and never fails the check. Not tested when neither metadata document has scopes_supported; N/A without a browser join, with auth.disabled set to true, with no issuer, or for a file declaring another draft

rows.title: Conversation entries
rows.pass_when: agent.protocols is a non-empty list, each entry with a type and an https endpoint. From Draft 1.0, each entry also has a description of what the agent at that endpoint can help with (spec 8.1)

rows.title: API entries
rows.pass_when: apis is a non-empty list, each entry with a type (openapi or mcp for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2, any type from 0.3), an https url and a description

rows.title: OpenAPI parses

request.condition: when the file lists OpenAPI documents, at most 3

rows.pass_when: Each listed OpenAPI document (the first 3) is OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1

rows.title: MCP resource metadata

request.condition: when the file lists MCP servers, at most 3

rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.3, the RFC 9728 protected resource metadata at each listed MCP server's own well-known URL (the first 3) names the server's url as its resource, and lists the issuer in authorization_servers when it lists any; a server whose metadata URL answers 404 offers no account access and is not counted. For a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2, the metadata lists auth.issuer in authorization_servers, and (0.2) includes ES256 when it lists dpop_signing_alg_values_supported

rows.title: Excluded tasks document

request.condition: when a file declaring 0.3 lists one

rows.pass_when: Draft 0.3: the excluded tasks document answers 200 with a JSON object whose tasks list gives each task a task phrase; an alternative has instructions or references, and an openapi or mcp reference names an API the file lists. A document past Ora's 100 KB read cap reads not tested, since the spec sets no size limit. N/A when the file lists none or declares another draft (from Draft 0.4 excluded tasks are served per Session, behind tasks.endpoint)

rows.title: Same MCP server everywhere
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: every MCP server poppy.json lists has a server card in the site's ARD catalog

rows.title: Same organization
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: the site's ARD catalog host names the same organization as poppy.json (display name, and the did:web domain)

rows.title: Domains covered

request.target: each other domain the issuer binds (poppy_domains, or protected_resources from Draft 0.3): /.well-known/poppy.json
request.condition: when the issuer binding holds and the issuer lists other domains, at most 3

rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: each other domain the issuer binds (the first 3) serves a poppy.json naming the same issuer, or from Draft 0.3 naming none; for a file declaring 0.2 or later a www. host counts as its own domain

rows.title: One issuer
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2, the site's protected resource metadata (auth.md) lists the PAP issuer in authorization_servers. N/A from Draft 0.3, whose issuer comes from that same metadata

rows.title: One metadata document
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2, the site serves one authorization server metadata document, the PAP issuer's. N/A from Draft 0.3, which allows several authorization servers

rows.title: Shared token endpoint lists both protocols' grants
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: where the PAP issuer also serves auth.md's agent_auth, grant_types_supported lists every grant both protocols send to its token endpoint (from Draft 0.3, PAP's are refresh_token and Mediated Sign-In's grant when listed)

rows.title: Consistent 401s
rows.pass_when: Ora consistency check, not a spec requirement: a recorded 401 challenge from a PAP MCP server points at the same resource metadata as T0-18

rows.title: Token endpoint rejects a junk grant

request.target: the token endpoint in the issuer's metadata
request.condition: when the file has an issuer whose metadata has a token endpoint on the scanned domain (or, for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2, on a bound issuer's domain)

rows.pass_when: Answers invalid_grant, invalid_client or unauthorized_client, or a DPoP proof error; a 403 extension_required reads not tested (for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2: invalid_client (401), invalid_grant (400) or a DPoP proof error (400)). Ora also passes invalid_request at any 4xx status, with an advisory note, and for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2 any of its codes at a status other than the one its spec 4.2 table lists

rows.title: Error bodies leak nothing
rows.pass_when: No error body a probe got back carries a stack trace

rows.title: Conversation endpoint refuses a request with no credentials

request.target: {endpoint}/ora_probe/events on one conversation endpoint that poppy.json lists for the poppy protocol (an entry without access signed_in first, then the first in alphabetical order); for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2, a POST to the endpoint itself

rows.pass_when: Answers 400 with invalid_session in a JSON body (for a file declaring 0.4 or later, a 400 version_unsupported reads not tested, since Poppy-Version may be checked first, and a 403 extension_required reads not tested from 0.3; from 0.3, a 401 asking for an account at an entry with access signed_in reads not tested, since that entry needs account access first and the spec does not order the two checks); for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2, 401 with a DPoP challenge; a conversation_not_found answer fails, since the endpoint looked the conversation up without a Session header, and for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2 offers no Bearer challenge (one offered next to DPoP still fails)

rows.title: MCP server challenges unauthenticated initialize

request.target: one MCP server that poppy.json lists (the first in alphabetical order)

rows.pass_when: Answers 401 with resource_metadata on every Bearer or DPoP challenge. For a file declaring 0.2: a Bearer challenge, plus a DPoP challenge when the server's RFC 9728 metadata lists DPoP algorithms, each with resource_metadata pointing at that metadata; for 0.1, a 401 when the metadata is at the well-known URI also passes. A server that completes initialize with no token, refuses it before any token check with 400 invalid_session (0.3 and later), 400 version_unsupported (0.4 and later), or 403 extension_required (in WWW-Authenticate for 0.3, in a JSON body from 0.4), or rejects it with the 400 and MCP error of a server that speaks only MCP 2026-07-28 has no 401 challenge to grade, so the row reads not tested

rows.title: Browser join page is safe to load

request.condition: when a file declaring 0.3 or later lists one

rows.pass_when: Answers 200 with a form holding a code, a cookie that ties the code to the browser (SameSite Strict or Lax, and a __Host- name, since spec 6 says other hosts on the domain must not be able to set the cookie and only that prefix ensures it), Cache-Control: no-store, frame-ancestors 'none' (or X-Frame-Options: DENY) and a Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy that severs the opener

rows.title: Browser endpoint rejects a junk join
rows.pass_when: Answers an error status and no cookie (a CDN or load balancer cookie, or one the response clears, does not count; for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2, 400 and no cookie)

rows.title: Browser join authorization requires a Session

request.condition: when a file declaring 0.3 or later lists one

rows.pass_when: Answers 400 invalid_session (a 400 invalid_request, a 403 extension_required, or for a file declaring 0.4 or later a 400 version_unsupported, reads not tested)

rows.title: Operations endpoint requires a token

request.target: the operations endpoint, with a made up operation id
request.condition: when a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2 advertises the operations extension

rows.pass_when: Answers 401, and for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2 offers no Bearer challenge (one offered next to DPoP still fails)

rows.title: Feedback endpoint requires a token

request.condition: when a file declaring 0.2 lists one

rows.pass_when: Answers 401 with a DPoP challenge, and for a file declaring 0.1 or 0.2 offers no Bearer challenge (one offered next to DPoP still fails)

rows.title: Protocol endpoints answer without a redirect
rows.pass_when: From Draft 0.2: every probed endpoint (token, conversation, MCP, operations, feedback, and from Draft 0.3 the browser join's /authorize; never the join page or form, whose success is a redirect) answers without a redirect, since an agent sends no token, Session header, DPoP proof, assertion or credentials to the URL a protocol endpoint redirects to. N/A for a file declaring 0.1, which ADV-REDIRECT grades

rows.title: Endpoint answers without a redirect
rows.pass_when: For a file declaring 0.1: every probed endpoint answers without a redirect, as the 0.1 guides recommend (each hop would need a fresh DPoP proof). N/A for a file declaring 0.2 or later, which T1-14 grades

rows.title: Call each read-only OpenAPI GET with no token, then with a valid signed-out token
rows.pass_when: Draft 0.2 plan, being rewritten for 1.0: Protected operations return 401 invalid_token without one; public ones behave the same either way

rows.title: Load the consent page for Ora's real client_id from a valid S256 request and inspect headers; never sign in
rows.pass_when: Draft 0.2 plan, being rewritten for 1.0: frame-ancestors CSP present

rows.title: Start a Session for U1
rows.pass_when: Draft 0.2 plan, being rewritten for 1.0: 200 with access_token, token_type: DPoP, expires_in > 0, session_id, signed_in: false, empty scope; Cache-Control: no-store

rows.title: Token lifetime
rows.pass_when: Draft 0.2 plan, being rewritten for 1.0: expires_in is hours, not days (≤ 24 h)

rows.title: Renew with session_id
rows.pass_when: Draft 0.2 plan, being rewritten for 1.0: New token, same session_id

rows.title: Nonce challenge
rows.pass_when: Draft 0.2 plan, being rewritten for 1.0: If use_dpop_nonce is returned, a retry with the DPoP-Nonce value succeeds

rows.title: Token request with no DPoP proof for an MCP server (resource = MCP url)
rows.pass_when: Draft 0.2 plan, being rewritten for 1.0: token_type: Bearer, accepted at that MCP server, when its protected resource metadata lists no DPoP algorithms; invalid_dpop_proof when it does

rows.pass_when: Draft 0.2 plan, being rewritten for 1.0: Requests with only Authorization + DPoP succeed
